title: Torrance Waterworks onramp - call notes & technical sketch
content:
Summary / context:
This is a raw capture from the 2025-09-18 kickoff call with Torrance Waterworks (municipal water utility). They want an LLM-enabled incident summarization + operator assistant for distributed water-quality sensors across remote pump stations. Primary ask: private deployment (VPC or on-prem) with strict data residency (city-owned), occasional air-gapped sites, and FOIA-sensitive logs. They want a low-friction trial to evaluate latency, cost, and offline resilience.

Call attendees (notes):
- Priya Nair (CTO) — owner for product requirements, FOIA/regulatory point
- Carlos Mendez (Infra lead) — network topology, field connectivity constraints
- Jordan Liu (Redwood SE) — solution design, trial scope
- Alyssa Reid (Redwood AE) — commercial / next steps
- Marcus Chen (Redwood SRE) — ops constraints, monitoring

Key user goals (plain):
- Summarize sensor events into short incident reports for on-call operators (1–3 sentences + severity)
- Provide chat-style assistant for operators to query recent events and evidence (with links to raw telemetry slices)
- Guarantee no telemetry leaves city VPC except model weights/updates under controlled process (customer consent)
- Offline mode: hubs with intermittent connectivity must still run inference locally for the last 24h of data

Non-functional constraints (important):
- FOIA: logs/notes must be exportable and auditable; system must support retention windows and redaction flags
- Network: several pump stations are on LTE with <1 Mbps uplink and high jitter; cannot rely on large KV-cache syncs often
- Ops: small team — wants simple rollback and single-click disable of remote agent
- Latency SLO for operator chat: target 500ms–1200ms for short summarization calls; batch telemetry processing can be looser (<=5s)

Technical gotchas / risk areas observed on call:
1) Air-gapped updates: Torrance wants ability to apply model/weights updates via USB or RGZ image for isolated hubs. We need a documented offline update flow and signed artifact verification.
2) KMS: they use Azure Key Vault for secrets. Private deployment must integrate with their KMS via customer-managed identity; no Redwood-managed keys.
3) FOIA + fallback: They explicitly forbid sending raw telemetry offsite. That rules out our usual fallback to hosted Redwood for degraded compute. Proposed pattern: deploy a small local fallback model artifact that can run on CPU/GPU in reduced quality mode (on-prem-only), and only if network is healthy allow richer analysis on a dedicated private cluster.
4) Bandwidth-sensitive prefix caching: continuous prefix/KV sync across distributed sites will eat significant uplink. Need to keep local caches independent and prioritize incremental syncs.
5) Tokenization cost for time-series metadata: will need to design compact prompt templates (structured summary + pointers to raw event IDs) to keep per-incident token spend low.

Model & infra sketch (quick, tentative):
- Trial cluster: 2x GPU nodes (customer suggested A10G-equivalent), 4 CPU workers for preprocessing. Region: customer VPC with private subnet.
- Local hub fallback: dockerized runtime (Redwood Private light) with a quantized 4-bit LLM variant (Llama2 small-ish or a fine-tuned distilled model) to run on CPU if necessary.
- Model routing policy: prefer private cluster (good perf) -> on-hub quantized model (if cluster unreachable) -> fail gracefully and return cached summary (if both unavailable).
- Caching: local per-hub KV cache for last 72 hours of conversations/events; periodic incremental delta backups to central private cluster when bandwidth permits.

Prompt / output expectations (from product):
- Incident summary format must be structured CSV-like for operator ingestion: severity | 1-line summary | timestamp | sensor-ids | evidence-links (keep short)
- Chat assistant should support a function call to request raw telemetry slices (time windows) via secure signed urls; those URLs must be generated and expire quickly.

Compliance / audit notes:
- Retention policy needs to be configurable per-data-type; FOIA export workflow must be plumbed into Redwood logs (audit entries for every generated summary + original event IDs).
- Must maintain per-request provenance metadata: model version, prompt template ID, route (cluster/hub/fallback), and user id.

Operational monitoring & SLOs:
- Instrument token counts, avg latency p50/p95, fallback rate (percent of requests which hit local quantized model), and bandwidth used for KV sync.
- Alerting: >5% fallback rate sustained for 10m -> page ops; high latency p95>2s -> degrade to summary-only mode.

Open questions (to resolve in tech deep-dive):
- Can Torrance accept any telemetry ever leaving their VPC for model updates/metric collection? (Priya: only anonymized aggregated metrics allowed; no raw payloads)
- Which machines at hubs can run GPU? If none, need robust CPU-only runtime & perf expectations.
- Who signs off on FOIA export process? Need legal contact for city.
- What's the expected incident frequency? This determines batching vs real-time tradeoffs.

Next steps & owners (short):
- Jordan (Redwood SE): schedule 90m technical deep-dive with Torrance infra + legal. Tentative window: 2025-09-25. (owner: Jordan)
- Marcus (SRE): draft a minimal trial infra blueprint (2-node private cluster + hub image build notes) and estimate cost ops. Deliver by 2025-09-22.
- Alyssa (AE): send trial agreement template and sensitive-data addendum; propose 8-week trial terms. (owner: Alyssa)
- Carlos (Torrance): provide network topology export and list of 6 pilot hubs + their connectivity profiles. Requested by 2025-09-24.
- Priya (Torrance): connect city legal for FOIA sign-off; provide contact. (owner: Priya)

Low-effort experiments to validate quickly (MVP ideas):
- Run a local-only POC: ship quantized model image + container to 2 pilot hubs, run a week of synthetic event summaries, measure latency and quality. This avoids VPC work and proves the offline flow.
- Create compact prompt templates (token budget <=256) and run cost/throughput estimate for 1k incidents/day.

Notes-to-self (SE):
- When building the hub image, include an offline updater that accepts a signed release bundle; document the exact verification steps (GPG + Redwood manifest).
- Prepare a short runbook for city ops on how to disable remote updates and revert to factory image.

Rough time estimates (ballpark):
- Minimal local-only POC: 2–3 weeks engineering + hub image prep + 1 week pilot run = ~5 weeks
- VPC-connected private cluster trial with basic KMS integration and observability: 4–6 weeks more

End of scratch capture.

(Formatting: messy; meant as internal scratchpad. Convert to formal brief once deep-dive answers are in.)
